headline: Army Sets 9 a.m. Iowa Detonation of Degraded Lead Azide
deck: A multi-agency evaluation led to approval of an in-place operation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, and an appeals court allowed the Army to proceed.
body: After a U.S. appeals court allowed the Army and Trump administration to proceed, the Army newly scheduled an in-place controlled detonation of degraded, crystallized lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant for Wednesday at about 9 a.m. CST. The Army said it announced the plans in close coordination with the Environmental Protection Agency, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Department of Health and Human Services, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and state and local emergency-management authorities. The scheduled detonation is the update from the paper’s 24 November coverage. [E1][E4]
A routine safety inspection found severe degradation and crystallization in about 68 drums holding more than 9,700 pounds of lead azide. [E2]

The Army said leadership approved a detonation by 71st Ordnance Group explosive-ordnance-disposal specialists after an evaluation by the ATF, EPA, Department of War Explosives Safety Board, Defense Threat Reduction Agency and Army Corps of Engineers, calling it the only viable method to permanently eliminate the hazard. [E3]
